title: Transfers of Financial Assets - ASC 860
learning_objectives: Apply sale vs secured borrowing test

content.fundamental_question: Is transfer a SALE or SECURED BORROWING?
sale_criteria_all_must_be_met: 2. Transferee has right to pledge or exchange assets (or if SPE, holders have that right)
3. Transferor does NOT maintain effective control through repurchase agreement or requirement to return specific assets
content.if_sale: Remove assets from balance sheet, recognize gain/loss
content.if_secured_borrowing: Assets remain on balance sheet, record liability

factoring_receivables.definition: Selling receivables to factor (financial institution) for cash

without_recourse.description: Factor assumes risk of uncollectible accounts
without_recourse.accounting: Treat as SALE (if meets sale criteria). Remove receivables, recognize loss equal to difference.

with_recourse.description: Transferor retains risk of uncollectible accounts (may have to buy back bad receivables)
with_recourse.accounting: May be sale or secured borrowing depending on sale criteria. If sale, recognize recourse liability at fair value.
with_recourse.typical_treatment: Often qualifies as sale but requires recourse liability recognition

accounting_for_sale.step_1: Allocate carrying amount of assets to portions sold and retained (if partial) based on fair values
accounting_for_sale.step_2: Recognize assets obtained and liabilities incurred at fair value
accounting_for_sale.step_3: Remove carrying amount of assets sold
accounting_for_sale.step_4: Recognize gain or loss = Proceeds + FV of assets/liabilities obtained - Carrying amount sold

servicing_assets_and_liabilities.when_arise: When transferor retains servicing responsibilities but doesn't receive adequate compensation (servicing liability) or receives more than adequate (servicing asset)
servicing_assets_and_liabilities.servicing_asset: If benefits of servicing > cost of servicing (transferor expects to profit from servicing)
servicing_assets_and_liabilities.servicing_liability: If cost of servicing > benefits (transferor expects to incur net cost)
servicing_assets_and_liabilities.measurement: Initially at fair value. Subsequently: Amortize in proportion to servicing income (asset) or expense (liability), or measure at fair value each period (election).

secured_borrowing_accounting.transferor: Assets remain on books. Record cash received as liability. Continue to recognize related revenues and expenses.
secured_borrowing_accounting.example: Transfer receivables as collateral for loan. DR Cash, CR Loan Payable. Keep receivables on books.

factoring_calculation_without_recourse.facts: Factor receivables (carrying $100K, FV $100K) without recourse. Receive cash $90K. Factor fee $10K.
factoring_calculation_without_recourse.analysis: Meets sale criteria (without recourse, factor assumes risk).
factoring_calculation_without_recourse.entry: DR Cash $90K, DR Loss on Sale $10K, CR Receivables $100K

factoring_calculation_with_recourse.facts: Factor receivables (carrying $100K) with recourse. Receive $92K cash. Recourse liability FV $3K. Factor fee $8K.
factoring_calculation_with_recourse.analysis: Assume meets sale criteria. Must recognize recourse liability.
factoring_calculation_with_recourse.entry: DR Cash $92K, DR Loss on Sale $5K, CR Receivables $100K, CR Recourse Liability $3K

partial_transfer_example.facts: Sell 80% of receivables (total CA $100K, FV $100K) for $75K. Retain 20% and servicing rights (FV $2K).
partial_transfer_example.allocation: 80% sold: CA $80K, proceeds $75K. 20% retained: CA $20K. Servicing asset $2K.
partial_transfer_example.entry: DR Cash $75K, DR Servicing Asset $2K, DR Loss $3K, CR Receivables $80K

transfers_to_qspe.historical: Qualified Special Purpose Entities (QSPEs) previously allowed off-balance-sheet treatment
transfers_to_qspe.current: QSPE concept eliminated by ASC 860 update. Most SPEs now consolidated if variable interest entity.

securitization.definition: Transfer receivables to SPE, which issues securities backed by receivables
securitization.accounting: If meets sale criteria, derecognize receivables. If transferor retains significant interest or control, may require consolidation of SPE (VIE rules).

cpa_exam_tips: Sale criteria: (1) Isolated, (2) Transferee can pledge/exchange, (3) No effective control retained
Without recourse: Usually sale (remove receivables, recognize loss)
With recourse: May be sale, must recognize recourse liability at FV
Secured borrowing: Keep assets on books, record liability
Servicing asset/liability: Recognize at FV if retain servicing responsibilities
Gain/loss = Proceeds + FV of assets/liabilities obtained - CA of assets sold

sale_vs_borrowing_test: 1. Check sale criteria (isolated, transferee can pledge, no effective control)
2. If all met → Sale (remove assets, recognize gain/loss)
3. If any NOT met → Secured borrowing (keep assets, record liability)
factoring_approach: Without recourse → Usually sale → DR Cash (proceeds), DR Loss (plug), CR Receivables (CA)
With recourse → Usually sale but add recourse liability → DR Cash, DR Loss (plug), CR Receivables, CR Recourse Liability (FV)
cpa_exam_strategies.gain_loss_calculation: Proceeds + FV of assets retained + FV of liabilities incurred - Carrying amount of assets transferred
common_mistakes: Assuming all factoring is sale (check sale criteria)
Forgetting recourse liability when factoring with recourse
Not allocating carrying amount when partial transfer
Confusing secured borrowing (assets stay on books) with sale (assets removed)

key_points: Sale vs secured borrowing: Check 3 criteria (isolated, transferee can pledge, no control)
If sale: Remove assets, recognize gain/loss
If secured borrowing: Keep assets on books, record liability
Without recourse: Usually sale, factor assumes risk
With recourse: May be sale, recognize recourse liability at FV
Servicing asset/liability: Recognize at FV if retain servicing
Gain/loss = Proceeds + FV obtained - CA transferred
